SOWK 201.description: This course introduces students to the history and contemporary context of the social work profession, including generalist practice and the role of advocacy. It emphasizes responses to current needs and changing contexts.
SOWK 201.subject: SOWK
SOWK 201.title: Introduction to Social Work

SOWK 222.description: This course introduces students to the historical and current context of social welfare policies and programs in the United States, including examination of social inequalities and the processes of social policy development.
SOWK 222.subject: SOWK
SOWK 222.title: Social Welfare Policies and Programs

SOWK 303.description: This course introduces the context for social work with children, youth, and families as well as specific theories, policies, programs, and services. Areas examined include antipoverty policies and programs, child welfare, education, behavioral health, healthcare, disabilities, and juvenile justice.
SOWK 303.subject: SOWK
SOWK 303.title: Social Work With Children, Youth, and Families

SOWK 304.description: This course introduces students to the context for social work with older adults, as well as specific theories, policies, programs, and services. Areas examined include the aging process, health and wellness, behavioral health, sexuality, work and retirement, bereavement, living arrangements and housing options, and social programs and policies targeting older adults.
SOWK 304.subject: SOWK
SOWK 304.title: Social Work With Older Adults and Families

SOWK 305.description: This course introduces anti-oppressive theoretical and applied approaches to understand and address intersections of gender and racial inequality. Social welfare policies and services available to women in contexts such as criminal justice, behavioral health, child welfare, and the military are examined.
SOWK 305.subject: SOWK
SOWK 305.title: Gender, Race and Social Justice

SOWK 307.description: This course introduces students to global dimensions of social inequality, beginning with the historical roots of global social inequality and moving through contemporary themes relevant to international social work practice from an anti-colonial perspective. Topics examined include human rights, gender-based violence, global health, climate change, and immigration/displacement.
SOWK 307.subject: SOWK
SOWK 307.title: Global Inequalities and Social Justice

SOWK 308.description: Exploration of how sport, recreation, and play can promote positive youth development. Based on an ecological perspective and a risk and resilience framework.
SOWK 308.subject: SOWK
SOWK 308.title: Promoting Positive Youth Development through Sport, Recreation, and Play

SOWK 309.description: This course will examine the grief and loss process that is part of everyday life. This course surveys the knowledge and skills of human service practice with people as they cope with life transitions.
SOWK 309.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 101, or SOCY 101, or SOWK 201.
SOWK 309.subject: SOWK
SOWK 309.title: Life Transitions: Loss and Grief

SOWK 311.description: This course introduces students to the context and mission of social work. It emphasizes the interactions between personal and professional values, ethical and professional behavior, and beginning engagement and interpersonal skills.
SOWK 311.subject: SOWK
SOWK 311.title: Foundations of Social Work Practice

SOWK 312.description: This course introduces students to engagement, assessment, intervention, and evaluation with individuals and families. It includes specific models and techniques of practice with an emphasis on managing barriers to change, client strengths, and understanding diversity and difference in practice.
SOWK 312.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 311.
SOWK 312.subject: SOWK
SOWK 312.title: Social Work Practice with Individuals and Families

SOWK 316.description: Introduction to perspectives on justice with the goal of developing a theoretically informed social justice framework and exploring the complexity of social justice. Selected social movements will be introduced and analyzed.
SOWK 316.subject: SOWK
SOWK 316.title: Social Justice and Social Movements

SOWK 317.description: Comprehensive introduction to spiritually sensitive social work; emphasizes reflective practice, assessment skills, and the integration of spirituality into professional social work.
SOWK 317.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 201 or SOWK 311.
SOWK 317.subject: SOWK
SOWK 317.title: Spirituality in Social Work

SOWK 318.description: Introduction to generalist social work case management models and skills with an emphasis on diverse and vulnerable populations.
SOWK 318.subject: SOWK
SOWK 318.title: Social Work Case Management

SOWK 319.description: Introduction to trauma-informed practice for various populations as well as specific theories and services. Areas examined include traumatic stress, grief reactions, cognitive, neurobiological/physiological, psychological, and ecological perspectives.
SOWK 319.subject: SOWK
SOWK 319.title: Trauma Informed Practice

SOWK 322.description: Knowledge, values, and skills for social work practitioners to analyze the political and ideological factors and outcomes of policy development, implementation, evaluation, and advocacy.
SOWK 322.subject: SOWK
SOWK 322.title: Social Policy Analysis

SOWK 331.description: Builds cultural competency through awareness, understanding, and skill necessary for proactive functioning in our diverse society with populations considered vulnerable and oppressed.
SOWK 331.subject: SOWK
SOWK 331.title: Diversity and Social Justice in Contemporary Society

SOWK 341.description: This course focuses on theories for understanding individual, family, and group behavior to better serve clients across settings. It emphasizes diversity, difference, and the advancement of human rights and social, economic, and environmental justice.
SOWK 341.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 201.
SOWK 341.subject: SOWK
SOWK 341.title: Theories for Understanding Individuals, Families, and Groups

SOWK 352.description: Foundational knowledge and skills for scientific inquiry and the use of quantitative and qualitative research to inform evidence-based practice.
SOWK 352.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: SOWK 201, SOWK 222 and select one course from the following: STAT 201 or higher, PSYC 227 or SOCY 220.
SOWK 352.subject: SOWK
SOWK 352.title: Social Work and Scientific Inquiry

SOWK 360.description: This course provides students with foundational knowledge about forced migration and the institutions of humanitarian aid that address forced migration. Students will learn about global theories of forced migration, humanitarian aid policy, empirical studies of humanitarian aid, refugee resettlement, and displacement, and evaluate biographies and literature on forced migration.
SOWK 360.subject: SOWK
SOWK 360.title: Refuge and Refugees

SOWK 368.description: An in-depth study of selected issues and social concerns related to being a generalist social worker. Content varies by title.
SOWK 368.subject: SOWK
SOWK 368.title: Special Topics in Social Work

SOWK 382.description: An initial application of generalist social work skills and theories taught in a controlled and planned classroom setting.
SOWK 382.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 311.
SOWK 382.subject: SOWK
SOWK 382.title: Introduction to Field Education

SOWK 404.description: A project-type study of selected issues, social concerns, and applications of behavioral implications for practice. May be repeated for credit when the topics covered or subject matter is different.
SOWK 404.subject: SOWK
SOWK 404.title: Current Issues in Social Welfare

SOWK 411.description: This course introduces students to engagement, assessment, intervention, and evaluation with treatment and task groups. It includes specific models and techniques of practice with an emphasis on group practice with diverse populations across practice settings.
SOWK 411.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 312.
SOWK 411.subject: SOWK
SOWK 411.title: Social Work Practice with Groups

SOWK 412.description: This course introduces students to engagement, assessment, intervention, and evaluation with organizations and communities. It includes specific models and techniques of practice with an emphasis on diversity, difference, and the advancement of human rights and social, economic, and environmental justice.
SOWK 412.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 411.
SOWK 412.subject: SOWK
SOWK 412.title: Social Work Practice with Organizations and Communities

SOWK 422.description: Knowledge and skills embedded in values of social and economic justice for all people across systems of all sizes that are essential in generalist practice.
SOWK 422.subject: SOWK
SOWK 422.title: Advocacy for Social and Economic Justice

SOWK 441.description: This course focuses on theories for understanding large social systems to better serve clients across settings. It emphasizes diversity, difference, and the advancement of human rights and social, economic, and environmental justice.
SOWK 441.subject: SOWK
SOWK 441.title: Theories for Understanding Organizations and Communities

SOWK 481.description: Application of generalist social work competencies, theories and code of ethics taught in the classroom in a community organizational setting.
SOWK 481.subject: SOWK
SOWK 481.title: Practicum I: Field Education

SOWK 482.description: Further application of the generalist social work skills and theories taught in the classroom in a controlled and planned setting.
SOWK 482.subject: SOWK
SOWK 482.title: Practicum II: Field Education

SOWK 483.description: Taken with the field practicum, this seminar facilitates student's integration of generalist practice knowledge with practice in a field agency.
SOWK 483.subject: SOWK
SOWK 483.title: Practicum Seminar

SOWK 484.description: Competent generalist social work practice demands integration of a wide range of theories, knowledge, skills, and values. This course is designed to draw on all previous courses and to engage students in integrating and applying all that they have learned.
SOWK 484.subject: SOWK
SOWK 484.title: Capstone

SOWK 668.description: Study of special populations, settings, and/or problems encountered by social workers and other human service professionals, and interventions and skills for dealing with them. May be repeated as content varies by title.
SOWK 668.subject: SOWK
SOWK 668.title: Special Topics in Social Work

SOWK 678.description: Foundation for beginning health professions students to gain an understanding of the complexities of the health care system through experiential activities conducted in interprofessional teams and the importance of interprofessional collaboration in order to improve the system.
SOWK 678.subject: SOWK
SOWK 678.title: Transforming Health Care for the Future

SOWK 679.description: Approaches for prevention of childhood obesity, using perspectives from public health, social work, exercise science, pharmacy, medicine, and behavioral nutrition. Training to teach diet/physical activity lessons in elementary school settings.
SOWK 679.subject: SOWK
SOWK 679.title: Addressing Childhood Obesity through Community Approaches

SOWK 701.description: Bridge course designed to prepare newly enrolled Advanced Standing MSW students for their Advanced Practice year of study for the MSW program.
SOWK 701.subject: SOWK
SOWK 701.title: Professional Development Bridge

SOWK 702.description: Prepare students to write effectively for professional practice in social work.
SOWK 702.subject: SOWK
SOWK 702.title: Writing for Professional Social Work Pratice

SOWK 703.description: This seminar is part of a collaborative school social work/law enforcement practicum immersion study. Permission of the instructor and concurrent enrollment in an instructor-approved field practicum is required.
SOWK 703.subject: SOWK
SOWK 703.title: Richland County Sheriff's Department School Practicum

SOWK 704.description: This course provides students with foundational knowledge for leading and managing nonprofit or nongovernmental organizations. The student will learn about governance, human resources, financial management, marketing, and planning and evaluation. In this class, the student will use theory to understand effective organizational practices in a modern era. This course counts as a practice elective.
SOWK 704.subject: SOWK
SOWK 704.title: Nonprofit Leadership

SOWK 705.description: Social work practice with families, parents, and couples, focused on family interventions and family therapy with culturally diverse and vulnerable family populations. This course counts as a practice elective.
SOWK 705.subject: SOWK
SOWK 705.title: Family Interventions and Family Therapy

SOWK 707.description: Integration of trauma into practice with children, youth, and families to recognize its prevalence, realize its impact, and respond sensitively and competently.
SOWK 707.subject: SOWK
SOWK 707.title: Trauma-Informed Practice with Children, Youth, and Families

SOWK 708.description: Integration of trauma into practice with adults and older adults to recognize its prevalence, realize its impact, and respond sensitively and competently.
SOWK 708.subject: SOWK
SOWK 708.title: Trauma-Informed Practice with Adults and Older Adults

SOWK 709.description: Designed to focus on trauma-informed, trauma responsive, and culturally sensitive engagement, assessment, intervention, and advocacy regarding collective experiences of trauma such as natural and environmental disasters, mass shootings, community violence, and war.
SOWK 709.subject: SOWK
SOWK 709.title: Collective Trauma and Recovery

SOWK 712.description: Study of institutions, communities, and organizations as social systems relevant to social work practice.
SOWK 712.subject: SOWK
SOWK 712.title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment I

SOWK 714.description: Diversity, strengths, needs, and responses of oppressed populations from a social justice perspective, with emphasis on experiential learning and implications for social work practice at all system levels.
SOWK 714.subject: SOWK
SOWK 714.title: Diversity and Social Justice Issues for Social Work Practice

SOWK 716.description: A systems approach is used to study the family and individual development. Cultural and structural variability are emphasized.
SOWK 716.subject: SOWK
SOWK 716.title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment II

SOWK 718.description: Integration and application of social work theories, skills, and values in preparation for the transition to professional practice.
SOWK 718.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time, Part-time, and Advanced Standing students: C or higher in SOWK 779, SOWK 783, and SOWK 792 or SOWK 793.
SOWK 718.subject: SOWK
SOWK 718.title: Systems Analysis of Social Work Practice

SOWK 722.description: Methods of social work intervention with individuals, families and groups within the social environment.
SOWK 722.subject: SOWK
SOWK 722.title: Social Work Practice with Individuals, Families and Small Groups

SOWK 726.description: An in-depth study of modalities for overseeing the delivery of direct services in social agencies. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 726.subject: SOWK
SOWK 726.title: Supervision and Case Consultation

SOWK 727.description: Examination of school social work services from a multi-level, ecological approach including the community, the school, the family, and the students. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 727.subject: SOWK
SOWK 727.title: Social Work in an Educational Setting

SOWK 728.description: Practice of social work case management with a special emphasis on case management for vulnerable populations. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 728.subject: SOWK
SOWK 728.title: Social Work Case Management

SOWK 729.description: Knowledge and skills for practice with cognitive behavior therapies. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 729.subject: SOWK
SOWK 729.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapies

SOWK 730.description: Integration and infusion of meaning of trauma into one’s practice so as to recognize its prevalence, realize its impact, and respond sensitively and competently. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 730.subject: SOWK
SOWK 730.title: Trauma-informed Social Work Practice

SOWK 731.description: Motivational interviewing strategies and advanced practice competencies within in a variety of social work practice settings. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 731.subject: SOWK
SOWK 731.title: Motivational Interviewing for Social Work Practice

SOWK 732.description: Social work practice in organizations and communities, especially skills in problem identification and solving.
SOWK 732.subject: SOWK
SOWK 732.title: Social Work Practice with Organizations and Communities

SOWK 735.description: Advanced social work practice with individuals focused on engagement, assessment, intervention planning and implementation, and practice evaluation for diverse clients.
SOWK 735.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in SOWK 722 and SOWK 732.
SOWK 735.subject: SOWK
SOWK 735.title: Advanced Social Work Practice with Individuals

SOWK 737.description: Foundation knowledge for practice with military and their families including information about military culture, values. An overview of military knowledge and history essential for working with this population, information about problems unique to the military, and the identification of treatment and community resources.
SOWK 737.subject: SOWK
SOWK 737.title: Overview of Social Work Practice with the Military, Veterans, and their Families

SOWK 738.description: Designed to provide state-of-the-art information about problems and disorders encounter by veterans and military personnel, including information about the signature injuries associated with current and past conflicts, as well as information about problems encountered in family life.
SOWK 738.subject: SOWK
SOWK 738.title: Military Mental Health and the Impact of Trauma

SOWK 739.description: Knowledge about intervention strategies with military members, veterans of the military and their families, including important knowledge to help social workers interface effectively with other medical and behavioral health professionals.
SOWK 739.subject: SOWK
SOWK 739.title: Intervention Strategies in Military Behavioral Health

SOWK 740.description: This course provides a framework for understanding social work and social justice issues with an emphasis on vulnerable populations in the areas of survival, protection, and promotion of human rights in China, India, the Middle East, Africa, and Central and South America.
SOWK 740.subject: SOWK
SOWK 740.title: International Social Work and Social Justice

SOWK 742.description: Analysis of social welfare policies, including their development, implementation, and evaluation.
SOWK 742.subject: SOWK
SOWK 742.title: Social Welfare Policy Analysis

SOWK 743.description: This course examines immigration policy in the contemporary U.S. context. It explores current policy debates in light migration research and theory, and aims to address the following questions: Why do people migrate? How do they adapt once they arrive? How does immigration impact receiving societies?
SOWK 743.subject: SOWK
SOWK 743.title: Immigration Policy

SOWK 744.description: Planning and program development through grant writing that can be generalized to any setting and relevant to social, community, and economic development as well as other areas of social work practice.
SOWK 744.subject: SOWK
SOWK 744.title: Grant Writing

SOWK 746.description: Course develops skills for effective social work practice within dynamic and multifaceted mental health settings. Substantive areas include role play, research informed practice and practice informed research, and reflective/reflexive practice. The primary goal is to produce practitioners capable of influencing mental health related practice paradigms, programs, services, interventions, and policies. This course qualifies as a Practice Elective.
SOWK 746.subject: SOWK
SOWK 746.title: Community Mental Health

SOWK 748.description: This course introduces students to crisis theory and intervention models for response to a variety of individual, family, and community crises. This course focuses on crisis theories, the tasks associated with crisis care, methods of intervention and the responses to specific crises.
SOWK 748.subject: SOWK
SOWK 748.title: Crisis Intervention

SOWK 749.description: Examines theories of practice and parenting interventions with strong empirical evidence for supporting positive youth development and preventing or ameliorating child and adolescent social, emotional, and behavioral challenges among diverse youth and parents.
SOWK 749.subject: SOWK
SOWK 749.title: Evidence Based Parenting Interventions Child Adolescent Social, Emotional, Behavioral Challenges

SOWK 751.description: Students are introduced to the unique dynamics of substance use among adolescent populations. Students gain foundational knowledge about adolescent development, substance use trends and prevalence among adolescent populations. Risk and protective factors are explored that impact adolescent substance use, and systems of care for this unique group.
SOWK 751.subject: SOWK
SOWK 751.title: Youth and Substance Use

SOWK 752.description: Knowledge and skills for substance abuse treatment for clients from diverse backgrounds with a focus on empirically based methods from a social work practice.
SOWK 752.subject: SOWK
SOWK 752.title: Social Work Intervention in Substance Abuse

SOWK 755.description: Advanced social work practice with organizations, including advanced knowledge, skills, values, and theories to engage, assess, intervention, and evaluation organizations.
SOWK 755.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in SOWK 722 and SOWK 732.
SOWK 755.subject: SOWK
SOWK 755.title: Advanced Social Work Practice with Organizations

SOWK 756.description: Explores values, addresses psychosocial issues and examines assessment and intervention tools important for practice with persons with disabilities, their families and the community.
SOWK 756.subject: SOWK
SOWK 756.title: Social Work Practice and Developmental Disabilities

SOWK 758.description: An examination of the dynamics of substance abuse and addictions including classification of drugs, models of addiction, etiology, assessment and diagnosis and evidence-based treatment practices. Family dynamics, special populations (e.g., women, African Americans, Military), and process addictions (e.g., gambling, sexual addiction, eating disorders) are also covered.
SOWK 758.subject: SOWK
SOWK 758.title: Family Dynamics and Substance Abuse

SOWK 759.description: This course introduces students to etiology, assessment, and diagnosis of child and adolescent mental health within the social work person-in-environment framework to understand the critical biopsychosocial influences on incidence and manifestation of the most commonly presented disorders and the differential effect of these factors on diverse and at-risk populations.
SOWK 759.subject: SOWK
SOWK 759.title: Psychopathology and Psychodiagnostics for Social Work Practice with Children and Adolescents

SOWK 760.description: This course introduces students to etiology, assessment, and diagnosis of adult and older adult mental health within the social work person-in-environment framework to understand the critical biopsychosocial influences on incidence and manifestation of the most commonly presented disorders and the differential effect of these factors on diverse and at-risk populations.
SOWK 760.subject: SOWK
SOWK 760.title: Psychopathology and Psychodiagnostics for Social Work Practice with Adults and Older Adults

SOWK 762.description: Losses encountered throughout the life cycle, normal and pathological grieving, and intervention techniques.
SOWK 762.subject: SOWK
SOWK 762.title: Loss, Grief, and Social Work Intervention

SOWK 765.description: Sexuality in the context of social functioning and its relationship to problems encountered by social work practitioners. Emphasis on problems of sexual oppression.
SOWK 765.subject: SOWK
SOWK 765.title: Sexuality Issues for Social Work Practice

SOWK 766.description: Advanced generalist social work practice with diverse family systems across the life span, focused on engagement, assessment, intervention, and evaluation processes.
SOWK 766.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in SOWK 722 and SOWK 732.
SOWK 766.subject: SOWK
SOWK 766.title: Advanced Social Work Practice with Families

SOWK 768.description: An in-depth study of selected issues, social concerns, and application of behavioral implications for practice. May be repeated as content varies by title.
SOWK 768.subject: SOWK
SOWK 768.title: Special Topics in Social Work

SOWK 769.description: Current knowledge about child abuse and neglect, including typologies, etiology, effects, and current practice interventions.
SOWK 769.subject: SOWK
SOWK 769.title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Child Abuse and Neglect

SOWK 771.description: Introduction to gerontology from the fields of demography, psychology, sociology, social welfare, and economics.
SOWK 771.subject: SOWK
SOWK 771.title: Psychosocial Approaches to Gerontology

SOWK 772.description: Examination of the policy/planning issues relating to older adults, including current trends in services, base for social service development, and evaluation of services for older adults.
SOWK 772.subject: SOWK
SOWK 772.title: Programs and Services for Older Adults

SOWK 775.description: Advanced social work practice with treatment and task groups, with a focus on engagement, assessment, intervention, evaluation, and policy practice.
SOWK 775.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in SOWK 722 and SOWK 732.
SOWK 775.subject: SOWK
SOWK 775.title: Advanced Social Work Practice with Groups

SOWK 776.description: Advanced generalist social work practice on a community system-level with a focus on engagement, assessment, intervention, and evaluation.
SOWK 776.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in SOWK 722 and SOWK 732.
SOWK 776.subject: SOWK
SOWK 776.title: Advanced Social Work Practice with Communities

SOWK 777.description: A theoretical background for specialized advanced social work practice incorporating social and behavioral science as a framework for analyzing evidence-based approaches for social work interventions.
SOWK 777.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time and Part-time Programs: C or better in SOWK 712, SOWK 714, SOWK 716, SOWK 781, and SOWK 791; Advanced Standing Program: None.
SOWK 777.subject: SOWK
SOWK 777.title: Advanced Theory for Social Work Practice

SOWK 778.description: Overview of the structure and functions of programs, policies, and systems in a specialized area of practice, including the history of policy development, the current policy environment, and the role of social workers and the social work profession in shaping and implementing policy in this area.
SOWK 778.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SOWK 777, SOWK 779, and SOWK 783.
SOWK 778.subject: SOWK
SOWK 778.title: Advanced Analysis of Social Policy, Programs, and Services

SOWK 779.description: Advanced direct practice in a specialized area with a focus on engagement, assessment, intervention planning and implementation, and practice evaluation for diverse client systems at multiple levels. Instructor permission required for non-MSW program students.
SOWK 779.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time and Part-time Programs: SOWK 722, SOWK 732, SOWK 742, SOWK 777, SOWK 782; Advanced Standing Program: SOWK 777.
SOWK 779.subject: SOWK
SOWK 779.title: Advanced Social Work Interventions

SOWK 781.description: An agency-based study of the community social welfare system and the social agency's place in delivery of services; a beginning involvement in agency practice.
SOWK 781.subject: SOWK
SOWK 781.title: Field Instruction I: Generalist Social Work Practice

SOWK 782.description: An agency-based study of the community social welfare system and the social agency's place in delivery of services; a beginning involvement in agency practice.
SOWK 782.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time and Extended-time Programs: C or better in SOWK 781.
SOWK 782.subject: SOWK
SOWK 782.title: Field Instruction II: Generalist Social Work Practice

SOWK 783.description: The third unit of field instruction is designed to support students’ integration of knowledge learned while taking advanced year practice courses. This is a pass or fail course.
SOWK 783.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time and Extended-time Programs: C or higher in SOWK 722, SOWK 732, SOWK 742, and SOWK 782; Advanced Standing Program: None.
SOWK 783.subject: SOWK
SOWK 783.title: Field Instruction III: Advanced Social Work Practice

SOWK 784.description: The fourth unit of field instruction is designed to support students’ integration of knowledge learned while taking advanced year practice courses. This is a pass or fail course.
SOWK 784.subject: SOWK
SOWK 784.title: Field Instruction IV: Advanced Social Work Practice

SOWK 791.description: Examination of social work research contexts, designs, and strategies.
SOWK 791.subject: SOWK
SOWK 791.title: Social Work Research Methodologies

SOWK 792.description: Examines measurement tools, evaluation designs, and advanced practice skills that can be used to evaluate social work practice with clients.
SOWK 792.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time and Part-time Programs: C or higher in SOWK 791; Advanced Standing Program: None.
SOWK 792.subject: SOWK
SOWK 792.title: Evaluation of Social Work Practice

SOWK 793.description: Examines methods that can be used to evaluate social work programs, policies, and practice.
SOWK 793.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Full-time and Part-time Programs: C or higher in SOWK 791; Advanced Standing Program: None.
SOWK 793.subject: SOWK
SOWK 793.title: Evaluation of Social Work Programs

SOWK 800.description: Examines across disciplines the theoretical and empirical foundations for social welfare and social work in historical, economic, social, and political contexts prior to the 20th century.
SOWK 800.subject: SOWK
SOWK 800.title: Intellectual Foundations of Social Welfare and Social Work I: Historical Roots

SOWK 801.description: Examines across disciplines the theoretical and empirical foundations of social welfare and social work in historical, economic, social, and political contexts from the early 20th century to the present.
SOWK 801.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in SOWK 800.
SOWK 801.subject: SOWK
SOWK 801.title: Intellectual Foundations of Social Welfare and Social Work II: Modern Developments

SOWK 802.description: Examines the process of developing theory-based welfare and social work scholarship from a variety of research approaches, focusing on conceptual model-building.
SOWK 802.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in SOWK 800 and SOWK 801.
SOWK 802.subject: SOWK
SOWK 802.title: Intellectual Foundations of Social Welfare and Social Work III: Conceptual Model-Building

SOWK 803.description: Examines the theoretical and empirical foundations of the profession of social work in historical, economic, social, and political contexts from the early 20th century to the present.
SOWK 803.subject: SOWK
SOWK 803.title: History of the Profession of Social Work

SOWK 804.description: Introduces the concept of theory and its relation to empirical investigation. Introduces middle range social science theories widely used for research in social work and social welfare.
SOWK 804.subject: SOWK
SOWK 804.title: Understanding and Using Social Science Theory

SOWK 805.description: Overview of a range of approaches to understanding what we can know as social scientists (ontology) and how we can know it (epistemology), and a deep dive into how these approaches play out in 1) understandings of scientific inquiry and core methodological concepts, 2) qualitative and quantitative methodological choices, and 3) the researcher’s role and positionality in advancing change-oriented knowledge claims.
SOWK 805.subject: SOWK
SOWK 805.title: Knowledge for Social Change: Ontology, Epistemology, and Methodology in Social Science Research

SOWK 806.description: Step-by-step approach to conducting a systematic review of scientific literature and summarizing findings in the format of a journal manuscript for potential publication.
SOWK 806.subject: SOWK
SOWK 806.title: Conducting a Systematic Literature Review for Publication

SOWK 811.description: Foundations of qualitative methods in social research with emphasis on intensive interviewing and grounded theory.
SOWK 811.subject: SOWK
SOWK 811.title: Qualitative Methods of Inquiry for Social Work Research

SOWK 822.description: Advanced study to evaluate and design measurement and instrumentation in social work research. Restricted to social work doctoral students.
SOWK 822.subject: SOWK
SOWK 822.title: Measurement and Instrument Design

SOWK 830.description: Doctoral-level course covering conceptual foundations and key processes and skills of community-engaged research for understanding and promoting social welfare and social change. Emphasis on engagement with community, collaboration, challenges, and ethics. Assignments include practical community-engaged research experience.
SOWK 830.subject: SOWK
SOWK 830.title: Community - Engaged Research for Social Welfare and Social Change

SOWK 831.description: Examines theoretical and practical foundations of providing leadership for social change through organizations, communities, public policies, and social norms.
SOWK 831.subject: SOWK
SOWK 831.title: Leadership for Social Change

SOWK 850.description: Examines issues related to making a successful transition from doctoral student to professional social work scholar. May be repeated for credit.
SOWK 850.subject: SOWK
SOWK 850.title: Social Work Doctoral Professional Seminar

SOWK 872.description: A wide range of supervised classroom, field, and other learning experiences designed to prepare the student for work as a social work educator.
SOWK 872.subject: SOWK
SOWK 872.title: Social Work Education Practicum

SOWK 889.description: Students acquire practical research experience, based on an individualized learning contract, under the supervision of a faculty member.
SOWK 889.subject: SOWK
SOWK 889.title: Doctoral Social Work Practicum

SOWK 890.description: Approaches to the organization, analysis, interpretation, and utilization of data sets available from social agency records or from existing empirical research.
SOWK 890.subject: SOWK
SOWK 890.title: Analysis of Social Work Data

SOWK 891.description: Analysis of complex data sets from social services agencies and other research sources.
SOWK 891.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in SOWK 890 or equivalent introductory statistics course approved by the Doctoral Program Committee.
SOWK 891.subject: SOWK
SOWK 891.title: Advanced Analysis of Social Work Data

SOWK 892.description: Advanced study of research methods commonly employed in the development of knowledge for social work practice and education. Critique of published social work research using a standardized critique model.
SOWK 892.subject: SOWK
SOWK 892.title: Design and Critical Analysis of Social Work Research

SOWK 894.description: A seminar designed to provide intensive faculty supervision and peer consultation to the doctoral student in the preparation of the dissertation proposal. Repeatable- 2 credits required for the doctoral program.
SOWK 894.subject: SOWK
SOWK 894.title: Planning and Design of Dissertation Research
